claims.conditions: No payment or donation flow tested; no paid plan verified

claims.wording: Depflush publishes its source under GPL-3.0; its name and icon are excluded from that licence.
claims.excerpt: The source code is released under the [GNU General Public License v3.0](LICENSE).
claims.supportingExcerpt: They are not licensed under the GPL.
claims.conditions: Do not extend source-code licence to website screenshots or trademarks

claims.wording: Dormant dependency discovery targets vendor next to composer.lock and node_modules next to package.json; the advertised default inactivity threshold is 12 months and is configurable.
claims.excerpt: vendor folders next to a composer.lock and node_modules next to a package.json, in projects you haven't changed for 12 months. You choose the threshold.
claims.conditions: FAQ says vendor, node_modules, var and .git are ignored for inactivity. Reinstallation depends on registries, credentials and compatible tooling; no guaranteed recovery

claims.wording: The documented Docker view preselects rebuildable cache/registry images, but leaves locally built images, stopped containers and orphaned volumes unticked with warnings.
claims.excerpt: Images you built yourself, stopped containers and orphaned volumes are listed with a warning and stay unticked.
claims.conditions: Docker must run for inspection; do not delete Docker.raw or imply a guaranteed reduction

claims.wording: Depflush documents item/path/size preview and confirmation, Trash by default, and optional permanent deletion in Settings.
claims.excerpt: Every item is listed with its path and size. You confirm the total before anything happens.
claims.supportingExcerpt: Files go to the Trash, so you can put them back. Switch to permanent deletion in Settings when you want the space right away.
claims.conditions: Not a safety guarantee; Trash bytes are not newly available disk space. No deletion performed

claims.wording: The vendor says scan and cleanup run locally, without an account, analytics or network calls; it also documents communication with the local Docker installation.
claims.excerpt: There is no account, no analytics and no crash reporting. The app only reads file sizes on your Mac and talks to your local Docker installation.
claims.conditions: Downloads, package restoration and registry pulls can require internet; do not claim all associated developer workflows are offline

claims.wording: Depflush documents a menu-bar free-space display and configurable low-space notifications, defaulting to 20 GB.
claims.excerpt: When it drops below the limit you set, 20 GB by default, you get a notification and can open the scan with one click.
claims.conditions: Not proof of per-app historical growth attribution or tested notification delivery

claims.wording: The official installation documentation says Depflush is not yet Apple-notarized; Full Disk Access is optional for Mail and iPhone backup size visibility.
claims.excerpt: Depflush is not yet notarized by Apple
claims.supportingExcerpt: Optional: grant Full Disk Access in Settings to see the size of Mail and iPhone backups as well.
claims.conditions: No binary signature inspected. Disclose warning; do not repeat protection-bypass instructions. Binary runtime requirements beyond macOS not verified

claims.wording: The vendor documents SHA-256 duplicate SQL-dump checking for dumps over 100 MB; exact duplicate photos/videos are separate from similar-photo detection.
claims.excerpt: Dumps over 100 MB are compared by size, then by SHA-256.
claims.supportingExcerpt: It compares photos and videos in Pictures, Movies, Documents, Desktop and Downloads byte for byte, so only true copies are listed, never similar-looking pictures.
claims.conditions: Do not certify deletion safety or duplicate accuracy without testing

claims.wording: Depflush's official screenshots are labelled sample data.
claims.excerpt: Safe items are ticked, anything you might still need is not, and each list says how to get it back. Sample data shown.
claims.conditions: Image capture date/version unknown; not our scan results

claims.wording: The official homepage links to cypriennkeneng/depflush; that repository links back to depflush.com and names Web Loupe (Cyprien Nkeneng).
claims.excerpt: Copyright © 2026 Web Loupe (Cyprien Nkeneng).
claims.conditions: Official snapshot links corroborate repository identity; no current alias established

claims.wording: Breathing Room, which we build, is a macOS 13+ preview; the identified release is 0.1.0-preview.1, advertised universal, Apple Development signed but not Developer ID signed or notarized, with physical Intel/clean-machine validation incomplete.
claims.excerpt: Published preview says **Apple Development signed, not Developer ID signed or notarized**.
claims.conditions: Register sections Preview, installation and runtime caveats and Unverified claims; not a new binary test

claims.wording: Breathing Room advertises a free local core and optional AI Care at $5 USD/month or $50 USD/year; hosted AI requires internet and authentication.
claims.excerpt: Confirmed advertised **$5 USD/month**, **$50 USD/year**.
claims.conditions: Renewal until cancellation; applicable checkout tax. Quotas/entitlement enforcement unverified; hosted requests may include paths, process/storage data

claims.wording: Breathing Room source implements storage views, grouped helper CPU/memory, sampled activity and exact-action review; this is not distributed-binary parity evidence.
claims.excerpt: Source implementation is not proof that every feature works in the distributed installer.
claims.conditions: Register Current capability matrix; do not promise attribution, speed or savings. Ruff automatic opt-in and daily exact approvals have different boundaries

claims.wording: Breathing Room discloses Python 3.10+ for inventory/legacy scripts, running-app requirements for daily care, website account-gated downloads and ungated public GitHub release downloads.
claims.excerpt: Python **3.10+** is a disclosed prerequisite for disk inventory and legacy scripts, not bundled.
claims.conditions: Register Preview, installation and runtime caveats and Pricing/access. No account creation or end-to-end hosted testing performed

claims.wording: Dusty by Toprak Yagcioglu is the MIT-licensed menu-bar Mac cleaner at toprak.sh/dusty, with source at yagcioglutoprak/dusty.
claims.excerpt: github.com/yagcioglutoprak/dusty

claims.wording: GitHub's latest public release is v2.1.0, published September 26, 2026; its README requires macOS 13 Ventura or later.
claims.excerpt: "tag_name":"v2.1.0"
claims.conditions: Not a binary or hardware test; architecture support not independently verified.

claims.wording: Dusty is offered free under MIT, with no trial, upsell or account according to its README.
claims.excerpt: Yes. MIT licensed, no trial, no upsell, no account.
claims.locator: README FAQ: Is it actually free?
claims.conditions: No currency/billing period applies to the documented free offer. Not Dusty Storage's paid offer.

claims.wording: Dusty documents scan, per-item review, confirmation, a dry-run switch, allowlisted targets and a local deletion log.
claims.excerpt:
Every path and its size are on screen before anything
  is deleted. Scanning never deletes.
claims.locator: README At a glance; How it works; Why you can trust it
claims.conditions: Do not turn vendor safety language into a guarantee; automatic mode is separately opt-in.

claims.wording: Dusty documents Safe, Developer and Deep levels; Developer includes package-manager and Xcode caches, while Deep includes stale project artifacts.
claims.excerpt: Three levels, from "do this anytime" to "look before you leap."
claims.conditions: Safe is a product label, not our safety judgment. Rebuild or re-download cost matters.

claims.wording: Dusty's documented stale-project review requires an adjacent manifest and checks user-file/git activity; it refuses artifacts if a project changes between scan and clean.
claims.excerpt: The tool's manifest has to sit right next to the artifact
claims.conditions: Documented examples are node_modules, Cargo target and virtualenv; not proof all languages/manifest versions are supported.

claims.wording: Dusty documents app memory totals including helpers and confirmed graceful quits with a brief Reopen window.
claims.excerpt:
Every app's total counts all the processes working for
  it
claims.conditions: Do not claim that Breathing Room alone groups helpers or that memory totals equal guaranteed reclaimed RAM.

claims.wording: Dusty documents background scans enabled every four hours by default and optional auto clean, disabled by default, on a schedule or free-space threshold.
claims.excerpt:
**Auto clean** (off by default) runs on a schedule (daily, weekly, or every
  two weeks)
claims.conditions: Safe or Developer cache scope; open apps skipped; Low Power Mode/dry run constraints documented. Do not claim recurring monitoring is absent.

claims.wording: Dusty's README documents scan insights and a disk-fill projection, alongside background scans.
claims.excerpt:
Insights only point; they never select or delete
anything.
claims.conditions: Not a validated prediction, complete file-activity history or proof of writer attribution.

claims.wording: Dusty's README describes a bundled CLI and Shortcuts actions, including read-only scan and memory queries.
claims.excerpt:
The `dusty` CLI ships
inside the app
claims.conditions: No commands executed; do not present shell output or tested tutorial.

claims.wording: Dusty says its DMG/Homebrew distribution is signed and notarized; source builds require Xcode 16 or later. Some Deep diagnostic paths need Full Disk Access.
claims.excerpt: It needs Xcode 16 or later (not just the Command Line Tools).
claims.locator: README Install, Full Disk Access, Build from source; release Install
claims.conditions: No downloaded installer, signature inspection, permissions change or launch. No Python requirement established for Dusty; do not claim binary runtime completeness.

claims.wording: Dusty's README describes a brief undo window but explicitly excludes emptying Trash, which is final; cleanup settings can purge Developer/Deep items after Undo.
claims.excerpt:
The one exception is emptying the Trash, which is final, just like in
Finder.
claims.locator: README FAQ What if I clean something I needed?; Settings cleanup defaults
claims.conditions: Homepage emphasizes Developer/Deep Trash handling; README has broader claims. Use the qualified wording, never universal undo, permanent recovery or guaranteed available-space gains.

claims.wording: Dusty documents local scanning/cleanup and says no account or telemetry; this research did not audit all network traffic or establish a hosted-AI feature.
claims.excerpt: Free, MIT licensed, no account, no telemetry.
claims.locator: README At a glance; homepage FAQ
claims.conditions: Updates can use network; not a blanket offline/privacy guarantee. Hosted AI status remains not verified.

claims.wording: Breathing Room's current identified preview is 0.1.0-preview.1 for macOS 13+, with Python 3.10+ required for inventory/legacy scripts; it is not notarized and physical Intel runtime testing remains unverified.
claims.excerpt:
Python is not
  bundled
claims.locator: README 59–72; capabilities preview table; package.json version cross-check
claims.conditions: Universal distribution is advertised, not validated hardware parity.

claims.wording: Breathing Room's core local app is free; optional AI Care is advertised at $5 USD/month or $50 USD/year. Hosted agent requests need internet and authentication.
claims.excerpt: **AI Care is optional: $5 USD/month or $50 USD/year.**
claims.locator: README 141–157; capabilities pricing and hosted boundary
claims.conditions: Renewing plans, applicable tax at checkout; no unlimited-AI promise or verified quota. Relevant paths/process/storage data may reach hosted service. Website download account gate differs from public GitHub download.

claims.wording: Breathing Room source provides category/app/project/folder storage views, app/helper CPU and memory, and sampled activity correlation.
claims.excerpt: These are observations, not a complete audit trail.
claims.conditions: Inventories may be partial; memory may count shared pages; inferred ownership and sampled I/O do not identify the writer of a particular file.

claims.wording: Breathing Room's daily care reuses exact saved path/method approvals while the app runs; interactive mode has a separate optional verified-Ruff-cache automatic Trash exception.
claims.excerpt:
Scheduled care cleans only exact locations and methods you
previously approved
claims.conditions: New daily actions wait for review; no wake-after-quit promise, no unconditional never-deletes-without-asking claim.

claims.wording: Breathing Room desktop source is Apache-2.0; this is not a licence to its hosted service or website.
claims.excerpt: Desktop source is Apache License 2.0 with NOTICE and preserved third-party attribution.
claims.conditions: Preserve applicable notices; no hosted-service entitlement implied.

claims.wording: Breathing Room source discovers developer caches and validates cleanup actions before constrained local execution.
claims.excerpt: Tools must exist and paths/methods must pass validation
claims.locator: capabilities.md Cleanup review/execution and Developer/builder cleanup rows
claims.conditions: Not every tool/cache version or distributed binary behavior was runtime tested.

claims.wording: The README documents Project Junk detection using project markers; dist and Pods require matching gitignore entries, and detected folders go to Trash.

claims.conditions: README behavior, not our execution test or release parity guarantee.

claims.wording: Disk Hogs documents Docker cleanup behind confirmations and simulator cleanup; the vendor says Docker volumes and the newest runtime per platform are not touched.
claims.excerpt: Prunes stopped containers, dangling images, and dangling build cache (each behind a confirmation) ... Docker volumes and the newest runtime for each platform are never touched
claims.conditions: Not permission to run these operations; not independently tested.

claims.wording: The vendor documents Trash-first deletion, dry-run preview, protected paths and exclusions; destructive exceptions such as Trash emptying and Shredder mean this is not universal recoverability.
claims.excerpt: every removal goes to the Trash by default, and a dry-run mode previews without touching anything; Shredder: Secure file erasure with standard, permanent, and secure-overwrite modes

claims.wording: Mac Sai documents local cleaning with optional update networking; no-telemetry assertions remain vendor claims, not an independent privacy audit.
claims.excerpt: two network paths, both optional and both read-only: ... optional Mac Sai update check ... user-driven check of other apps' Sparkle feeds

claims.wording: The README describes menu-bar CPU, memory, disk, battery and network statistics plus cache-growth recommendations, so do not claim Mac Sai has no monitoring.
claims.excerpt: Live CPU / memory / disk / battery; Recommendations: actionable, dismissible tips
claims.conditions: Per-app/helper grouping and historical writer attribution not verified.
